title: Methionine Cycle Flux
pm_id: BRS2-FM1-PM4
mission: 'Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.'
parent_fm: BRS2(FM1)
parent_brs: BRS2
summary: 'The methionine cycle forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine, transfers its methyl group, and hydrolyses S-adenosylhomocysteine to adenosine and homocysteine. Homocysteine is then remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine. SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate influence that split. Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine, while transsulfuration is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Metabolite concentrations describe pool state, not the branch rates.'

intervention_breakdown: Food-State Dominant
timing_specific: 'No'
dose_sensitivity: 'Methionine, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and riboflavin participate in the cycle. No ordinary-diet dose-response for human remethylation or transsulfuration rates is established.'
cofactors:

### Overview

The methionine cycle forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine, transfers its methyl group, and hydrolyses S-adenosylhomocysteine to adenosine and homocysteine. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) Homocysteine is then remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate influence that split. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine, while transsulfuration is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Metabolite concentrations describe pool state, not the branch rates. [[13]](#pm-ref-13)

- **Benefits:** Maintaining methionine-cycle flux lets cells keep donating methyl groups while directing sulfur toward cysteine. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) That coordination helps keep methylation and sulfur exit together.
- **Implementation Notes:** Methionine, dietary protein, vitamin B9 (folate), vitamin B12 (cobalamin), vitamin B6, and vitamin B2 (riboflavin) are the provision routes. [[6]](#pm-ref-6) [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Folic acid and vitamin B12 can lower blood homocysteine, and moderate vitamin B6 restriction can raise cystathionine, without a shown change in those branch rates. [[6]](#pm-ref-6) [[13]](#pm-ref-13)
- **Biological Relevance:** [SAMe formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis), each remethylation reaction, and the [transsulfuration enzyme steps](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) are neighbouring mechanisms. [[12]](#pm-ref-12)

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Methyl-group use and sulfur exit meet at homocysteine. What matters is how that intermediate is divided between return to methionine and transsulfuration, with SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors of the split.

<div class="brs-fm-hub-item" data-brs-fm-hub>
<div class="brs-fm-hub-shell">
<button type="button" class="brs-fm-hub-summary" aria-expanded="false">

<div class="brs-fm-hub-panel" hidden>

#### (From methionine to homocysteine)

Methionine is converted to S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the principal methyl donor. After the methyl group is transferred, S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) is hydrolysed to adenosine and homocysteine. Blocking that hydrolysis can affect methylation of phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules together [Chiang et al. (1996) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)].

#### (The regulated split)

Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine back to methionine. Transsulfuration, which converts homocysteine to cystathionine and onward toward cysteine, occurs in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Regulation is the distribution of homocysteine between those exits. SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate are effectors of that distribution [Finkelstein (1998) [[12]](#pm-ref-12)]. Human postprandial studies can measure the same partition as remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration rates [Lamers et al. (2011) [[13]](#pm-ref-13)].

#### (Concentrations and rates)

Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine concentration, and vitamin B12 adds a further concentration reduction, while added vitamin B6 does not [Collaboration (1998) [[6]](#pm-ref-6)]. A small trial also reported lower plasma homocysteine after vitamin B12, fish oil, or both [Huang et al. (2015) [[11]](#pm-ref-11)]. In the tracer study, cystathionine concentration rose during vitamin B6 restriction while the mean total transsulfuration rate did not [[13]](#pm-ref-13). A concentration change is a different result from a branch rate.

#### (Boundaries of the mechanism)

This mechanism is the integrated throughput and the split at homocysteine. Formation of SAM is [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). Folate- and vitamin B12-dependent remethylation is [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation). Betaine-dependent remethylation is [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation). The transsulfuration reactions are [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway). Methionine-restriction experiments in ageing models, and homocysteine associations with dementia or ADHD, do not show that changing these rates treats a cognitive or attention disorder [Fanti et al. (2026) [[3]](#pm-ref-3); Luzzi et al. (2022) [[8]](#pm-ref-8); Lukovac et al. (2024) [[9]](#pm-ref-9)].

#### (Integration within methylation cycle efficiency)

SAM synthesis feeds this throughput. Remethylation returns homocysteine to methionine, and transsulfuration is the catabolic exit. Downstream methyl acceptors include phospholipids, proteins, DNA and RNA [Chiang et al. (1996) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)]. The parent account of methylation cycle efficiency is [BRS2(FM1) — Methylation Cycle Efficiency](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-methylation-cycle-efficiency).

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

A controlled human tracer study found unchanged mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and transsulfuration rates during moderate vitamin B6 restriction, despite sharply reduced plasma PLP and increased cystathionine concentration. [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Pathway reviews provide the regulatory context for these measured branch rates. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) The combined evidence shows why an altered intermediate concentration cannot be treated as an equivalent change in overall cycle flux; individual responses and the restriction conditions limit generalisation.

### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships

Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function.

- [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) — Remethylates homocysteine to methionine and thereby carries one recycling exit. The split between that exit and transsulfuration is the upstream allocation.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) — Remethylates homocysteine to methionine by a betaine-dependent route that runs parallel to folate-dependent recycling and stays separate from transsulfuration.
- [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis) — Produces SAM from methionine and ATP. That SAM is the methyl donor consumed as throughput moves from methyl transfer to homocysteine and the branch.
- [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) — Carries homocysteine onward to cystathionine and cysteine after the branch has directed it into transsulfuration, which is the catabolic exit rather than the recycling arm.

## 7. Phenome Connections

summary: >-

  pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange.
  Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models;
  glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological
  routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement.

scientific_findings:
  - id: PM1-F1
    finding_label: Tight junctions govern selective paracellular permeability
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: >-
      Intestinal epithelial tight junctions form regulated pore and leak pathways that determine selective
      paracellular passage.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports the PM boundary around epithelial gate function. Downstream microbial-product containment
      and systemic inflammation remain outside it.
    finding_statement: >-
      Intestinal tight-junction structure and regulation determine selective paracellular permeability, while
      epithelial injury can create a distinct unrestricted permeability pathway.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      An authoritative mechanistic review distinguishes tight-junction-dependent pore and leak pathways from
      unrestricted flux caused by epithelial damage. In a mouse pneumonia model, increased permeability and
      claudin-2 were attenuated by oral LGG, providing intervention evidence that barrier permeability and
      junction-associated biology can move together under pathological conditions.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The review establishes mechanism rather than dietary responsiveness. The LGG experiment was performed in
      young mice with experimental Pseudomonas pneumonia, not in healthy humans, and does not establish a
      generic fermented-food effect.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Chanez-Paredes and Turner (2023)
        citation_key: chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#chanez_paredes_paracellular_2023
        data_level: Mechanistic
        evidence_source: bounded-external-search
        directional_finding: >-
          Tight junctions define size- and charge-selective pore and leak pathways; epithelial damage produces
          a separate unrestricted pathway.
      - label: Khailova et al. (2017)
        citation_key: khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        href: /docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#khailova_lactobacillus_2017
        data_level: Animal Data
        evidence_source: repository-inherited
        directional_finding: >-
          Oral LGG attenuated pneumonia-induced intestinal permeability and claudin-2 elevation and supported
          mucin expression in mice.
  - id: PM1-F2
    finding_label: Butyrate can support epithelial tight-junction assembly
    presentation: mechanistic-basis
    fm_rollup: false
    finding_summary: Microbial fermentation products, especially butyrate, can act directly on epithelial barrier biology.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      This supports a Direct butyrate relationship and a Derived fermentable-fibre provision relationship,
      with microbiota and fibre-specific limitations.
    finding_statement: >-
      Butyrate can function as an epithelial metabolic substrate and promote intestinal tight-junction
      assembly, while fermentable dietary fibre lies upstream as microbial substrate provision for
      short-chain-fatty-acid production.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In Caco-2 monolayers, physiological butyrate increased transepithelial resistance, reduced inulin
      permeability and accelerated tight-junction assembly alongside AMPK activation. A broader review links
      microbial fermentation of dietary substrates to short-chain-fatty-acid production and intestinal barrier
      effects.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      The direct assembly experiment is an immortalised epithelial-cell model. Fibre-to-butyrate conversion
      varies by fibre structure and microbial ecology, and neither source establishes a universal human intake
      threshold, a generic effect of all fibre, or oral butyrate as necessary treatment.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Peng et al. (2009)

        data_level: Mechanistic

          assembly in Caco-2 monolayers.

        data_level: Mechanistic

  - id: PM1-F3
    finding_label: Barrier markers and attention-related symptoms are associated, not causal
    presentation: phenome-relationship
    primary_phenome: Focus / Attention Stability
    finding_summary: >-
      One small cross-sectional ADHD study linked serum zonulin with hyperactivity, but it did not establish a
      causal tight-junction-to-attention pathway.
    finding_interpretation: >-
      The evidence is compatible with the proposed relationship but is too indirect to show that changing PM1
      changes attention stability.
    finding_statement: >-
      Current human evidence provides only indirect observational support for a relationship between
      intestinal barrier biology and attention-related symptoms.
    synthesised_evidence_confidence: not-yet-scored
    synthesis: >-
      In children with ADHD, serum zonulin was independently associated with hyperactivity and social-function
      scores. A separate microbiota study found lower Faecalibacterium abundance associated with parent-rated
      ADHD symptoms, but it did not measure barrier function. Together these studies support hypothesis
      generation, not a PM1-specific causal relationship.
    synthesis_limitations: >-
      Both studies are small and cross-sectional. Serum zonulin is an indirect permeability marker; neither
      study manipulated or directly quantified tight-junction integrity, and neither demonstrates that PM1
      changes attention outcomes.
    evidence_considered:
      - label: Özyurt et al. (2018)

## BRS5-1-1 - Gut Barrier / Tight Junction Integrity


## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported. Dietary inputs are the principal group displayed here, within the study-specific boundaries. Comparative dominance is not established.

### Overview

The gut lining is a selective gate. Tight junctions, the seals between its cells, control which materials pass between them. Maintaining that selectivity helps protect the body while allowing normal exchange. Butyrate, cellular zinc and retinoid signalling affect epithelial functions in experimental models; glutamine has a condition-specific human permeability result. These findings identify different biological routes rather than a universal gut-repair supplement. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

- **Benefits:** Selective permeability helps limit inappropriate passage across the gut lining; symptom benefits from supplementation are specific to the populations studied.
- **Implementation Notes:** Fermentable substrates can supply microbial butyrate. Nutrient adequacy differs from extra-intake benefit; the glutamine trial concerned postinfectious diarrhoea-predominant IBS with confirmed hyperpermeability.
- **Biological Relevance:** This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

↑ tight-junction strength; ↓ permeability

Cellular zinc supports junction-protein maintenance; retinoic acid influences epithelial differentiation and selective permeability. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Biological process

The zinc result supports a bounded cellular requirement. Retinoid biology cannot be simplified to lower permeability in every context. [[8]](#pm-ref-8)

#### Mechanism Boundary

This PM concerns epithelial junction regulation. Mucus-specific microbial effects belong to PM3 and bioactive endotoxin containment to PM2. Lower electrical resistance may reflect selective ion permeability rather than unrestricted leakage.

#### Integration

This PM contributes its specific process to its parent FM. Shared inputs do not merge distinct jobs or prove an integrated clinical outcome.

## BRS5-1-2 - LPS / Endotoxin Containment


## 1. Mission & Overview

### Mission

Limit host exposure to bacterial endotoxin and related inflammatory microbial products.

**Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported — Dietary Requirements is the strongest implemented lever set assessed here. Selection is provisional while dietary-protocol practices are reviewed; comparative superiority and clinical benefit are not established.

### Overview

Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), often called bacterial endotoxin, is a component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. The intestine encounters these bacterial products continually. Their movement into the body and persistence in an active form help determine the pressure placed on immune regulation. This PM concerns limiting that active exposure: barrier containment, lipid-associated transport and enzymatic inactivation contribute different parts of the process. Specific meal and fermentable-input studies identify possible dietary levers, while microbial composition and inflammation alone do not tell us how much endotoxin reached the host. [[9]](#pm-ref-9) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

- **Benefits:** Restricting inappropriate bioactive exposure helps prevent persistent microbial stimulation; effective defence also requires recovery from immune tolerance. [[19]](#pm-ref-19)
- **Implementation Notes:** Meal composition and preparation are testable routes; the available acute comparisons and mouse fibre protocols do not establish a routine intake prescription. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) [[11]](#pm-ref-11)
- **Biological Relevance:** This containment biology connects BRS5’s intestinal interface to BRS3 inflammatory responses, without equating a circulating LPS measurement with cognitive benefit.

## 2. Primary Biological Effects

Restriction of microbial-product entry; modification of lipid-associated transport; substrate-dependent microbial-product inactivation; limitation of persistent bioactive exposure.

## 4. Mechanistic Basis

### Summary

Host exposure reflects entry, distribution, inactivation and clearance, rather than microbiome abundance alone.

#### Transport and inactivation

Junction permeability contributes one entry route. Chylomicron-associated transport provides another; experimental inhibition distinguishes it from paracellular leak. Intestinal alkaline phosphatase acts on particular substrates, whereas AOAH removes secondary acyl chains from LPS after exposure. [[9]](#pm-ref-9) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) [[19]](#pm-ref-19)

#### Mechanism Boundary

Structural barrier maintenance belongs to PM1. SCFA production and signalling belong to PM5; the relevant containment consequence must be independently established here. Circulating LPS, LBP, GlycA, permeability probes and cytokines are different endpoints. General inflammation reduction is not a containment assay.

#### Integration

[BRS5-FM1-PM1 — Epithelial Barrier Integrity](/docs/biological-targets/brs5/fm1/brs5-fm1-pm1-gut-barrier-tight-junction-integrity) supplies structural context. [BRS3-FM1-PM2 — Gut-Derived Inflammatory Signalling](/docs/biological-targets/brs3/fm1/brs3-fm1-pm2-gut-derived-inflammatory-signalling) concerns the downstream load and response. No upstream pool or constituent is inherited automatically.

### 4.1 Scientific Findings

#### Summary

Defined meal and diet studies support context-dependent endotoxin changes. Human oligofructose evidence adds a longer exposure result to mouse fermentable-input findings. Whole-pattern effects differ by assay and population: a prudent-pattern study changed endotoxin activity, whereas Mediterranean/Healthy Eating interventions did not change mean LBP. Enzyme chemistry also limits universal detoxification claims. These findings do not establish a single intake prescription or cognitive benefit.
